blocks: Description: In the Session View, files dropped together normally stack down one track; with the key held they spread across tracks in one row. It works for audio and MIDI files, not Live Clips. See Ableton/Live/UG/07 Session View/04 Setting Up the Session View Grid and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/15 Session View.
Drop several browser files into the Session View as one scene across tracks Card

Description: Duplicates Arrangement clips or time, Session clips or scenes, notes, devices or a take lane, which the comping list calls Duplicate Selected Take Lane. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/05 Editing and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/17 Comping.
Place a copy of the selection right after it Card
Repeat the selected span of time right after itself across every Arrangement track Card
Repeat the selected span of time right after itself across every Arrangement track Card

Description: In the Arrangement View, inserts a copy of the selected time after the selection on every track and pushes the rest of the song later. See Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/11 Using the Time Commands and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/16 Arrangement View.

Description: Some editing shortcuts in the Session View act across all tracks with Shift added to them. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/05 Editing.

Extend an editing shortcut to a span of time across every track Card

Description: In the Arrangement View, Shift turns an edit into its time command, such as Cmd+Shift+D for Duplicate Time. See Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/11 Using the Time Commands and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/05 Editing.

Description: With part of an automation or clip envelope selected, Option makes the edit act on that part of the envelope only. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/05 Editing.

Description: Sets the Control Bar's global Ableton/Live/UI/Control-Bar/Menu/Quantization to 1/8, so launched clips and scenes start on the next eighth note. See Ableton/Live/UG/16 Launching Clips/04 Clip Launch Quantization and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/14 Global Quantization.
Set global launch quantization to an eighth note Card

Description: Opens the Export Audio/Video dialog, which renders the Arrangement selection, or the whole Arrangement, after the effects and mixer. See Ableton/Live/UG/05 Managing Files and Sets/01 Sample Files/03 Exporting Audio and Video and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/03 Working with Sets and the Program.
Render the Set to an audio or video file Card
Save the selected MIDI clip as a MIDI file Card
Save the selected MIDI clip as a MIDI file Card

Description: Exports the selected MIDI clip as a Standard MIDI File for use in other programs. See Ableton/Live/UG/05 Managing Files and Sets/02 MIDI Files/01 Exporting MIDI Files and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/03 Working with Sets and the Program.
Save the selected MIDI clip as a MIDI file Card
Drag a control or breakpoint in finer steps Card
Drag a control or breakpoint in finer steps Card

Description: Gives finer control over a knob, slider or envelope breakpoint while you drag it; on a breakpoint it also locks horizontal movement. See Ableton/Live/UG/26 Automation/07 Editing Automation/01 Editing Breakpoints and Segments, Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/06 Adjusting Values and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/07 Commands for Breakpoint Envelopes.
Drag a control or breakpoint in finer steps Card

Fit a clip's content into the Clip View editor's height Card

Description: In the Sample Editor or the MIDI Note Editor, zooms vertically so the waveform or the notes fill the editor; in the Arrangement View the key is Optimize Arrangement Height. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/11 Clip View Sample Editor and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/12 Clip View MIDI Note Editor.
Fit a clip's content into the Clip View editor's height Card
Fit a clip's whole length into the Clip View editor's width Card
Fit a clip's whole length into the Clip View editor's width Card

Description: In the Sample Editor or the MIDI Note Editor, zooms horizontally until the clip's content fits; in the Arrangement View the key is Optimize Arrangement Width. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/11 Clip View Sample Editor and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/12 Clip View MIDI Note Editor.
Fit a clip's whole length into the Clip View editor's width Card
Stretch or squeeze the selected notes to fill the time selection Card
Stretch or squeeze the selected notes to fill the time selection Card
Description: In the MIDI Note Editor, scales the selected notes in time so they span the selected range. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/12 Clip View MIDI Note Editor.
Stretch or squeeze the selected notes to fill the time selection Card
Switch the grid between fixed and zoom-adaptive spacing Card
Switch the grid between fixed and zoom-adaptive spacing Card

Description: With an adaptive grid, the spacing follows the zoom level; a fixed grid keeps its spacing. The same command is in the Options menu. See Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/10 Using the Editing Grid and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/13 Grid Snapping and Drawing.
Switch the grid between fixed and zoom-adaptive spacing Card
Fold or unfold the selected Arrangement tracks Card
Shortcut: U, or Left / Right on a track title bar
Fold or unfold the selected Arrangement tracks Card

Description: In the Arrangement View, unfolding shows a track's clips tall enough to select time inside them, and folding shrinks it to a thin row; on a Group Track it collapses or expands the group, which the track commands list as Collapse/Expand Grouped Tracks. See Ableton/Live/UG/06 Arrangement View/09 Selecting Clips and Time, Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/16 Arrangement View and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/19 Commands for Tracks.
Fold or unfold the selected Arrangement tracks Card
Move on to the next part of a bars-beats-sixteenths value while typing Card
Move on to the next part of a bars-beats-sixteenths value while typing Card
Description: In a position or length field, such as the Arrangement Position, jumps from bars to beats to sixteenths. See Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/06 Adjusting Values.
Move on to the next part of a bars-beats-sixteenths value while typing Card
Wrap the selected devices in a Rack Card
Wrap the selected devices in a Rack Card

Description: In the Device View, groups the selected devices into an Instrument, Audio Effect or MIDI Effect Rack; grouping a Rack again nests it. See Ableton/Live/UG/25 Racks/02 Creating Racks and Ableton/Live/UG/42 Keyboard Shortcuts/04 Working with Devices and Plug-Ins.
